blocks.source: 【作曲講座】主旋律を作る
blocks.translation: [Composition Guide] Creating the Main Melody

blocks.source: では、Dominoを起動して実際にＲＰＧっぽいフィールド曲を作ってみましょう。別に何の曲でもよいのですが、フィールドが比較的楽かなあと。フィールド曲というのは戦闘曲と並んでＲＰＧっぽさの象徴ですしね。なおかつ、戦闘曲のように激しくないので作りやすいはずです。
blocks.translation: Now, let's launch Domino and actually try making an RPG-style field theme. It doesn't really matter what kind of song we make, but I thought a field theme would be relatively easy. Field themes, along with battle themes, are symbols of the RPG style, after all. Also, since they're not as intense as battle themes, they should be easier to make.

blocks.source: テンポの調整
blocks.translation: Adjusting the Tempo

blocks.source: テンポを設定します。『Conductor』と書いてあるトラックを選択してください。「いきなりトラックとか言われても何のことやねん」とか思われたかもしれませんが、画面左のアレです。
blocks.translation: Let's set the tempo. Select the track labeled “Conductor.” You may be thinking, “What do you mean by a track all of a sudden?” It's that thing on the left side of the screen.

blocks.source: フィールド曲ならテンポは１２０～１３０ぐらいが標準的かと思います。初期状態の１２０でとりあえずは問題ありません。後でいくらでも調整できます。
blocks.translation: For a field theme, I think a tempo of around 120–130 is standard. The initial setting of 120 is fine for now. You can adjust it as much as you like later.

blocks.source: メロディの打ち込み
blocks.translation: Entering the Melody

blocks.source: 主旋律（メインメロディ）から作成します。『CH01』とあるトラックを選択してください。『System Setup』とあるトラックは文字通りセットアップ用の処理を行うところなので、そのままにしておいてください。
blocks.translation: We'll start by creating the main melody. Select the track labeled “CH01.” The track labeled “System Setup” is where setup processing is performed, just as its name suggests, so leave it as is.

blocks.source: 今回のところは主旋律から作ります。もっとも、作曲する際『何から作るか？』というのは自由です。ベースからでもコード進行からでもリズムからでも、何だって構いません。色んなやり方をしたほうが、曲のバリエーションも増えると思います。
blocks.translation: This time, we'll start with the main melody. However, when composing, what you start with is entirely up to you. You can start with the bass, chord progression, or rhythm—anything is fine. I think using various approaches will also increase the variety of your songs.

blocks.source: 最初のところは初期化命令が入っています。なので一小節目は空けることが多いです。僕の場合、空白が大きくできるのが嫌なので『編集＞拍子』のところをいじって一小節目を短縮しています。
blocks.translation: The beginning contains initialization commands. For that reason, the first measure is often left empty. In my case, I don't like having a large blank space, so I adjust the settings under “Edit > Time Signature” to shorten the first measure.

blocks.source: よく分かんなかったら、そのままでいいです。とにかく最初の小節は空けておいて、『２』と書いてある小節から音符を配置するようにしてください。
blocks.translation: If you don't understand it well, you can leave it as is. In any case, leave the first measure empty and place notes starting in the measure labeled “2.”

blocks.source: 楽器は好みでよいですが、最初は音がはっきりと鳴るような聞き取りやすいものがお勧め。『049のStrings』なんかよさ気です。
blocks.translation: You can choose any instrument you like, but at first I recommend one with a clear, easy-to-hear sound. “049 Strings” seems like a good choice.

blocks.source: 楽器の変更は「挿入＞プログラムチェンジ」です。最初からある『PC:～』とある命令がそれなので、それをダブルクリックして変更しても構いません。
blocks.translation: To change the instrument, select “Insert > Program Change.” The command labeled “PC:~” that is there from the start is the one you need, so you can also double-click it to change it.

blocks.source: 初めてという方は色々と鳴らしてみて遊んでみるとよいでしょう。
blocks.translation: If this is your first time, try playing various sounds and experimenting.

blocks.source: 調
blocks.translation: Keys

blocks.source: いざ主旋律！ メロディを打ち込んでいきます。
blocks.translation: Now for the main melody! Let's enter the melody.

blocks.source: どの『調』で作るかというのがポイントになりますが、とりあえずは『イ短調』から始めることをお勧めします。
blocks.translation: Which key you compose in is important, but for now I recommend starting with A minor.

blocks.source: 「そもそも調って何？」という人も多いと思いますが、雑に説明します。
blocks.translation: Many people may be wondering, “What is a key in the first place?” Let me give you a rough explanation.

blocks.source: 長調：明るい。コミカル。緊張感がない。
blocks.translation: Major: Bright. Comical. Lacks tension.

blocks.source: 短調：暗い。カッコいい。哀愁。緊張感がある。
blocks.translation: Minor: Dark. Cool. Melancholic. Has tension.

blocks.source: 学校では「長調は明るい」「短調は暗い」みたく習ったかもしれませんが、若干誤解を招く気がします。「長調は明るい」「暗い曲は短調」は確かにそうだと思います。ただ「短調は暗い」は必ずしも成り立ちません。
blocks.translation: You may have learned at school that “major is bright” and “minor is dark,” but I feel that this can be somewhat misleading. I do think that “major is bright” and “dark songs are minor” are generally true. However, “minor is dark” is not necessarily true.

blocks.source: 上に挙げた通り、カッコいいゲーム音楽には短調の曲がとても多いのです。カッコよくてノリが良い曲が短調だったりすることはよくあります。戦闘曲なんかは大抵が短調です。
blocks.translation: As mentioned above, many cool video game music tracks are in minor keys. It's quite common for cool, upbeat songs to be in minor keys. Battle themes, in particular, are usually in minor keys.

blocks.source: フィールド曲については長調・短調の両方が使われますが、短調のほうが多数派です。ドラクエやＦＦのフィールド曲も短調が優勢です。「ＦＦ５の序盤」なんかは長調ですね。……たぶん。
blocks.translation: Both major and minor keys are used for field themes, but minor is more common. The field themes from Dragon Quest and Final Fantasy also tend to be in minor keys. “The early part of FF5” is in a major key, I think… probably.

blocks.source: というわけで『イ短調』から始まるフィールド曲を作ってみましょう。
blocks.translation: So let's try creating a field theme that starts in A minor.

blocks.source: なぜに『ロ短調』や『ハ短調』ではなく、『イ短調』かというと打つのが楽だからです。
blocks.translation: The reason we're using A minor instead of B minor or C minor is that it's easier to enter.

blocks.source: Dominoの五線譜部分を眺めてみると、白い部分と薄い青色の部分に分かれているのが確認できると思います。ピアノでいうと、白い部分が白い鍵盤です。薄い青色の部分が黒い鍵盤です。
blocks.translation: If you look at the staff notation area in Domino, you'll notice that it's divided into white and light blue sections. On a piano, the white sections correspond to the white keys, while the light blue sections correspond to the black keys.

blocks.source: イ短調とはラを基準とした短調のことなので、ラの音から始めて白い部分に音符を打ち込んでいけばＯＫなのです。薄い青色――つまり＃や♭は入らないので分かりやすいというわけです。
blocks.translation: A minor is a minor key based on A, so you can simply start with A and enter notes in the white sections. Since there are no light blue notes—in other words, no sharps or flats—it's easy to understand.

blocks.source: 一応、説明しておくと『ラ』と『イ』は同じ音を表しています。小学校で習ったはずですが、忘れたという人は以下の表をどうぞ。アメリカ式もコード進行を表す時に使ったりしますね。
blocks.translation: For the sake of completeness, “La” and “I” represent the same note. You probably learned this in elementary school, but if you’ve forgotten, here’s the table below. The American system is also sometimes used to represent chord progressions.

blocks.source: フランス式
blocks.translation: French notation

blocks.source: ラ
blocks.translation: A

blocks.source: シ
blocks.translation: B

blocks.source: ド
blocks.translation: C

blocks.source: レ
blocks.translation: D

blocks.source: ミ
blocks.translation: E

blocks.source: ソ
blocks.translation: G

blocks.source: アメリカ式
blocks.translation: American notation

blocks.source: Ａ
blocks.translation: A

blocks.source: Ｂ
blocks.translation: B

blocks.source: Ｃ
blocks.translation: C

blocks.source: Ｄ
blocks.translation: D

blocks.source: Ｅ
blocks.translation: E

blocks.source: Ｆ
blocks.translation: F

blocks.source: Ｇ
blocks.translation: G

blocks.source: 日本式
blocks.translation: Japanese notation

blocks.source: イ
blocks.translation: A

blocks.source: ロ
blocks.translation: B

blocks.source: ハ
blocks.translation: C

blocks.source: ニ
blocks.translation: D

blocks.source: ホ
blocks.translation: E

blocks.source: ヘ
blocks.translation: F

blocks.source: ト
blocks.translation: G

blocks.source: なので、イ短調はフランスではラ短調、アメリカではＡ短調となります。
blocks.translation: Therefore, A minor is called A minor in French notation and A minor in American notation.

blocks.source: 素人目に統一しろよとツッコミたくなりますが、複数の外国から取り入れた弊害のようです。お陰様で日本の音楽教育が無駄に難しくなっていますね。
blocks.translation: From a layperson's perspective, you might want to say, “Can't you just standardize this?” but it seems to be a consequence of adopting systems from multiple foreign countries. Thanks to that, music education in Japan has become unnecessarily complicated.

blocks.source: 打ち込んでみる
blocks.translation: Trying It Out

blocks.source: では、ラから始まるメロディを８小節ほど打ち込んでみてください。
blocks.translation: Now, try entering a melody that starts with A, about eight measures long.

blocks.source: いきなり戸惑うかもしれませんが、まずはやってみることです。
blocks.translation: You may feel confused at first, but the important thing is to give it a try.

blocks.source: 頭の中に浮かんだメロディを配置と演奏を繰り返しながら再現しましょう。思い浮かばなくとも、しょせんパターンは有限です。適当にやっていればそのうちできます。
blocks.translation: Recreate the melody that comes to mind by repeatedly entering and playing it. Even if nothing comes to mind, there are only so many patterns, after all. If you experiment randomly, you'll eventually come up with something.

blocks.source: とにかく８小節です。８小節が無理なら、まずは４小節作ってそれをコピペして繰り返してください。ちょこっと修正すれば、８小節のメロディができあがります。
blocks.translation: In any case, aim for eight measures. If eight measures is too difficult, start by making four measures, then copy and paste them to repeat the pattern. With a few minor adjustments, you'll have an eight-measure melody.

blocks.source: 始まりの部分なので、平坦で面白みのないメロディでも大丈夫です。返ってそのほうが後のサビとのメリハリがついてよいかもしれません。
blocks.translation: Since this is the opening section, it’s fine for the melody to be plain and uninteresting. In fact, that might be better, as it will create more contrast with the chorus later on.

blocks.source: はい。僕も適当に打ち込んでみました。５分ぐらいで適当にパパッとやってます。画像が小さくて見づらいと思うのでクリックして拡大すると分かりやすいです。できれば真似しないで、自分なりのメロディを打ち込んでください。
blocks.translation: Yes. I also entered one fairly randomly. I just slapped it together in about five minutes. The image is small and may be hard to see, so click it to enlarge it for a clearer view. If possible, don’t imitate it—try entering a melody of your own.

blocks.source: では、さらに後ろへ８小節を追加し１６小節にします。とりあえず最初の８小節をコピペしてください。最後らへんだけ適当に変えて、一区切りついた感じにします。
blocks.translation: Next, let’s add another 8 bars at the end, making 16 bars in total. For now, copy and paste the first 8 bars. Make a few arbitrary changes toward the end to give it a sense of closure.

blocks.source: 最後の３小節だけ変えてみました。
blocks.translation: I changed only the last 3 bars.

blocks.source: そんなんでいいのかって言えばそんなんでいいです。音楽とは繰り返しです。全部の小節を一から打ち込む必要はありません。
blocks.translation: If you’re wondering whether that’s really okay, yes, it’s perfectly fine. Music is repetition. You don’t need to enter every bar from scratch.

blocks.source: 次にサビを作ります。また８小節追加です。
blocks.translation: Next, we’ll create the chorus. Add another 8 bars.

blocks.source: 盛り上がる部分なのでそれっぽくしましょう。さっきより音程が上がっています。楽器もそれまでとは変えてみるとよいかもしれません。
blocks.translation: Since this is the climactic section, let’s make it sound the part. The pitch is higher than before. It might also be a good idea to change the instruments from those used up to this point.

blocks.source: 後ろの４小節が前半４小節のコピペ改変だったりしますが、そんな感じで大丈夫です。音楽において繰り返しを多用するのは当たり前のことです。
blocks.translation: The last 4 bars are modified copies of the first 4, but that’s perfectly fine. Making extensive use of repetition is perfectly normal in music.

blocks.source: イ短調のままでもよいのですが、せっかくなので『ハ長調』に転調しています。といっても難しいことではなく、ドから始まるメロディにするだけです。イ短調と使う音階は全く同じです。イ短調とハ長調の相互の転調はよく使われます。
blocks.translation: It would be fine to keep it in A minor, but since we have the opportunity, I modulated to C major. It’s not difficult; you simply make the melody start on C. The scale used is exactly the same as in A minor. Modulating between A minor and C major is common.

blocks.source: 跳躍進行
blocks.translation: Melodic Leaps

blocks.source: サビを盛り上げるコツは跳躍進行にあります。「ド→ミ」のように二音以上上がる進行を跳躍進行といいます。「ド→レ」「レ→ド」というような平坦なメロディばかりだと印象の強い曲を作ることは難しいです。
blocks.translation: The key to building up the chorus lies in melodic leaps. A progression that rises by two or more notes, such as “C → E,” is called a melodic leap. It’s difficult to create a memorable song if the melody consists only of plain progressions such as “C → D” and “D → C.”

blocks.source: 盛り上がりに乏しいと感じたならば、大胆な跳躍を掛けてみましょう。
blocks.translation: If it feels lacking in excitement, try making a bold leap.

blocks.source: どことなく明るく希望あふれるメロディになりました。これが長調に転調した効果です。
blocks.translation: The melody has become somewhat brighter and filled with hope. This is the effect of modulating to a major key.

blocks.source: これで最後です。サビの続きを８小節追加しましょう。こちらもコピペ改変でやってもいいですが、少し違うメロディにしてみました。
blocks.translation: This is the last part. Let’s add another 8 bars to continue the chorus. You could also modify a copy here, but I tried making the melody a little different.

blocks.source: これにて主旋律は終わりです。……といっても、ゲーム音楽ならループさせるのが普通なので、そこまで終わりっぽいメロディにする必要はありませんが。
blocks.translation: That concludes the main melody. …That said, looping is standard for game music, so you don’t need to make the melody sound quite so much like an ending.

blocks.source: 実際にループさせてみて、自然な感じになっているか確かめてください。
blocks.translation: Try looping it and check whether it sounds natural.

blocks.source: ループのやり方は以下を参考にどうぞ。
blocks.translation: Refer to the following for instructions on looping.

blocks.source: http://wikiwiki.jp/tkbsoft/?domino%2FFAQ#jf68742c
blocks.translation: http://wikiwiki.jp/tkbsoft/?domino%2FFAQ#jf68742c

blocks.source: 上にも書いていましたがツクールで演奏する際に、ループさせるには『ＣＣ１１１（コントロールチェンジ111番）』なる命令をループの戻り位置へと挿入する必要があります。ウディタもＣＣ１１１に対応してるらしいです。
blocks.translation: As I mentioned above, when playing it in RPG Maker, you need to insert a command called “CC111 (Control Change 111)” at the position where the loop returns. Apparently, WOLF RPG Editor also supports CC111.

blocks.source: そこには書いてませんが、挿入する箇所は先頭のトラックである必要があります。『System Setup』を開いて挿入しましょう。
blocks.translation: I didn’t mention it there, but the insertion point must be in the first track. Open “System Setup” and insert it there.

blocks.source: また、ＣＣ１１１できちんとループさせるには、曲の終了位置を正しく指定している必要もあります。以下を参考にしてください。この辺の情報って意外と分かりにくいんですよね。
blocks.translation: Also, for CC111 to loop the song properly, you must specify the song’s end position correctly. Please refer to the following. Information about this area is surprisingly difficult to understand.

blocks.source: http://mimikopi.nomaki.jp/midi/002/end/
blocks.translation: http://mimikopi.nomaki.jp/midi/002/end/

blocks.source: なお、ループさせた際は楽器や音量などの情報は初期化されませんので、ご注意ください。ループで戻ってきた位置より後ろにそれらの命令を挿入したほうがよいです。
blocks.translation: Please note that information such as the instrument and volume is not reset when the song loops. It is better to insert those commands after the position where the loop returns.

blocks.source: これが現段階での成果物です。まだまだ寂しい感じがしますね。次回以降で段々ゴージャスになるようにしていきますので、乞うご期待ください。
blocks.translation: This is the result at this stage. It still feels rather sparse. I’ll gradually make it more lavish in the upcoming installments, so please look forward to it.

blocks.source: TestField_MainMelody.mid
blocks.translation: TestField_MainMelody.mid

blocks.source: あっ、忘れてましたがＭＩＤＩファイルの保存は『ファイル＞SMF書き出し』で行います。
blocks.translation: Oh, I almost forgot: save the MIDI file using “File > SMF Export.”

blocks.source: 普通に『上書き保存』や『名前を付けて保存』をした場合はdms形式で保存されます。これはDomino専用のデータファイルなので、打ち込み時の設定情報も含めて保存されます。制作時は便利ですが、他では演奏できませんので、ご注意です。
blocks.translation: If you simply use “Save” or “Save As,” it will be saved in DMS format. This is a data file format exclusive to Domino, so it saves the configuration information used when entering the notes as well. It’s convenient during production, but it cannot be played elsewhere, so please be careful.

texts.というわけで『イ短調』から始まるフィールド曲を作ってみましょう。: So let's try creating a field theme that starts in A minor.
texts.なぜに『ロ短調』や『ハ短調』ではなく、『イ短調』かというと打つのが楽だからです。: The reason we're using A minor instead of B minor or C minor is that it's easier to enter.
texts.Dominoの五線譜部分を眺めてみると、白い部分と薄い青色の部分に分かれているの: If you look at the staff notation area in Domino, you'll notice that it's divided into white and light blue sections. On a piano, the white sections correspond to the white keys, while the light blue sections correspond to the black keys.
texts.イ短調とはラを基準とした短調のことなので、ラの音から始めて白い部分に音符を打ち込: A minor is a minor key based on A, so you can simply start with A and enter notes in the white sections. Since there are no light blue notes—in other words, no sharps or flats—it's easy to understand.
texts.一応、説明しておくと『ラ』と『イ』は同じ音を表しています。小学校で習ったはずです: For the sake of completeness, “La” and “I” represent the same note. You probably learned this in elementary school, but if you’ve forgotten, here’s the table below. The American system is also sometimes used to represent chord progressions.
texts.なので、イ短調はフランスではラ短調、アメリカではＡ短調となります。: Therefore, A minor is called A minor in French notation and A minor in American notation.
texts.素人目に統一しろよとツッコミたくなりますが、複数の外国から取り入れた弊害のようで: From a layperson's perspective, you might want to say, “Can't you just standardize this?” but it seems to be a consequence of adopting systems from multiple foreign countries. Thanks to that, music education in Japan has become unnecessarily complicated.
texts.では、ラから始まるメロディを８小節ほど打ち込んでみてください。: Now, try entering a melody that starts with A, about eight measures long.
texts.いきなり戸惑うかもしれませんが、まずはやってみることです。: You may feel confused at first, but the important thing is to give it a try.
texts.頭の中に浮かんだメロディを配置と演奏を繰り返しながら再現しましょう。思い浮かばな: Recreate the melody that comes to mind by repeatedly entering and playing it. Even if nothing comes to mind, there are only so many patterns, after all. If you experiment randomly, you'll eventually come up with something.
texts.とにかく８小節です。８小節が無理なら、まずは４小節作ってそれをコピペして繰り返し: In any case, aim for eight measures. If eight measures is too difficult, start by making four measures, then copy and paste them to repeat the pattern. With a few minor adjustments, you'll have an eight-measure melody.
texts.始まりの部分なので、平坦で面白みのないメロディでも大丈夫です。返ってそのほうが後: Since this is the opening section, it’s fine for the melody to be plain and uninteresting. In fact, that might be better, as it will create more contrast with the chorus later on.
texts.はい。僕も適当に打ち込んでみました。５分ぐらいで適当にパパッとやってます。画像が: Yes. I also entered one fairly randomly. I just slapped it together in about five minutes. The image is small and may be hard to see, so click it to enlarge it for a clearer view. If possible, don’t imitate it—try entering a melody of your own.
texts.では、さらに後ろへ８小節を追加し１６小節にします。とりあえず最初の８小節をコピペ: Next, let’s add another 8 bars at the end, making 16 bars in total. For now, copy and paste the first 8 bars. Make a few arbitrary changes toward the end to give it a sense of closure.
texts.最後の３小節だけ変えてみました。: I changed only the last 3 bars.
texts.そんなんでいいのかって言えばそんなんでいいです。音楽とは繰り返しです。全部の小節: If you’re wondering whether that’s really okay, yes, it’s perfectly fine. Music is repetition. You don’t need to enter every bar from scratch.
texts.次にサビを作ります。また８小節追加です。: Next, we’ll create the chorus. Add another 8 bars.
texts.盛り上がる部分なのでそれっぽくしましょう。さっきより音程が上がっています。楽器も: Since this is the climactic section, let’s make it sound the part. The pitch is higher than before. It might also be a good idea to change the instruments from those used up to this point.
texts.後ろの４小節が前半４小節のコピペ改変だったりしますが、そんな感じで大丈夫です。音: The last 4 bars are modified copies of the first 4, but that’s perfectly fine. Making extensive use of repetition is perfectly normal in music.
texts.イ短調のままでもよいのですが、せっかくなので『ハ長調』に転調しています。といって: It would be fine to keep it in A minor, but since we have the opportunity, I modulated to C major. It’s not difficult; you simply make the melody start on C. The scale used is exactly the same as in A minor. Modulating between A minor and C major is common.
texts.サビを盛り上げるコツは跳躍進行にあります。「ド→ミ」のように二音以上上がる進行を: The key to building up the chorus lies in melodic leaps. A progression that rises by two or more notes, such as “C → E,” is called a melodic leap. It’s difficult to create a memorable song if the melody consists only of plain progressions such as “C → D” and “D → C.”
texts.盛り上がりに乏しいと感じたならば、大胆な跳躍を掛けてみましょう。: If it feels lacking in excitement, try making a bold leap.
texts.どことなく明るく希望あふれるメロディになりました。これが長調に転調した効果です。: The melody has become somewhat brighter and filled with hope. This is the effect of modulating to a major key.
texts.これで最後です。サビの続きを８小節追加しましょう。こちらもコピペ改変でやってもい: This is the last part. Let’s add another 8 bars to continue the chorus. You could also modify a copy here, but I tried making the melody a little different.
texts.これにて主旋律は終わりです。……といっても、ゲーム音楽ならループさせるのが普通な: That concludes the main melody. …That said, looping is standard for game music, so you don’t need to make the melody sound quite so much like an ending.
texts.実際にループさせてみて、自然な感じになっているか確かめてください。: Try looping it and check whether it sounds natural.
texts.ループのやり方は以下を参考にどうぞ。: Refer to the following for instructions on looping.
texts.上にも書いていましたがツクールで演奏する際に、ループさせるには『ＣＣ１１１（コン: As I mentioned above, when playing it in RPG Maker, you need to insert a command called “CC111 (Control Change 111)” at the position where the loop returns. Apparently, WOLF RPG Editor also supports CC111.
texts.そこには書いてませんが、挿入する箇所は先頭のトラックである必要があります。『Sy: I didn’t mention it there, but the insertion point must be in the first track. Open “System Setup” and insert it there.
texts.また、ＣＣ１１１できちんとループさせるには、曲の終了位置を正しく指定している必要: Also, for CC111 to loop the song properly, you must specify the song’s end position correctly. Please refer to the following. Information about this area is surprisingly difficult to understand.
texts.なお、ループさせた際は楽器や音量などの情報は初期化されませんので、ご注意ください: Please note that information such as the instrument and volume is not reset when the song loops. It is better to insert those commands after the position where the loop returns.
texts.これが現段階での成果物です。まだまだ寂しい感じがしますね。次回以降で段々ゴージャ: This is the result at this stage. It still feels rather sparse. I’ll gradually make it more lavish in the upcoming installments, so please look forward to it.
texts.あっ、忘れてましたがＭＩＤＩファイルの保存は『ファイル＞SMF書き出し』で行いま: Oh, I almost forgot: save the MIDI file using “File > SMF Export.”
texts.普通に『上書き保存』や『名前を付けて保存』をした場合はdms形式で保存されます。: If you simply use “Save” or “Save As,” it will be saved in DMS format. This is a data file format exclusive to Domino, so it saves the configuration information used when entering the notes as well. It’s convenient during production, but it cannot be played elsewhere, so please be careful.
